citation: Yamaguchi S, Mitsui S, Yan L, Yagita K, Miyake S, Okamura H. Role of DBP in the circadian oscillatory mechanism. Molecular and Cellular Biology. 2000;20(13):4773-4781. doi:10.1128/MCB.20.13.4773-4781.2000.
description: This paper showed that mouse Dbp transcription is activated by CLOCK-BMAL1 through E-boxes and repressed by PER/CRY proteins. It supports the expectation that loss of BMAL1 activity should reduce Dbp and other E-box circadian output transcripts.

citation: Ripperger JA, Schibler U. Rhythmic CLOCK-BMAL1 binding to multiple E-box motifs drives circadian Dbp transcription and chromatin transitions. Nature Genetics. 2006;38(3):369-374. doi:10.1038/ng1738.
description: This study documented rhythmic binding of BMAL1 and CLOCK at multiple E-boxes in the mouse Dbp locus and associated chromatin activation. It is direct support for lower Dbp when BMAL1/CLOCK-dependent activation is lost.

citation: Schneikert J, Grohmann A, Behrens J. Truncated APC regulates the transcriptional activity of beta-catenin in a cell cycle dependent manner. Human Molecular Genetics. 2007;16(2):199-209. doi:10.1093/hmg/ddl464.
description: RNA interference against APC in colon cancer cells increased beta-catenin-dependent reporter activity and stimulated AXIN2/conductin expression. This provides target-specific support for APC loss increasing beta-catenin transcriptional output.

citation: Katoh M. Multi-layered prevention and treatment of chronic inflammation, organ fibrosis and cancer associated with canonical WNT/beta-catenin signaling activation. International Journal of Molecular Medicine. 2018;42(2):713-725. doi:10.3892/ijmm.2018.3689.
description: This review summarizes APC as a beta-catenin destruction-complex component and lists AXIN2, NKD1, NOTUM, LEF1, and other genes as representative beta-catenin targets. It supplies the downstream leg of the APC-to-Wnt-feedback chain used for APC responses.

citation: Schule M, Butto T, Dewi S, Schlichtholz L, Strand S, Gerber S, Endres K, Schweiger S, Winter J. mTOR Driven Gene Transcription Is Required for Cholesterol Production in Neurons of the Developing Cerebral Cortex. International Journal of Molecular Sciences. 2021;22(11):6034. doi:10.3390/ijms22116034.
description: This mouse-neuron study found sterol and cholesterol biosynthesis genes to be transcriptionally regulated by mTORC1 signaling in primary neurons and developing cerebral cortex. Because TSC2 restrains mTORC1, it supports the prediction that Tsc2 loss increases sterol-biosynthetic transcripts.

citation: Dahlqvist J, Torma H, Badhai J, Dahl N. siRNA silencing of proteasome maturation protein (POMP) activates the unfolded protein response and constitutes a model for KLICK genodermatosis. PLOS ONE. 2012;7(1):e29471. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0029471.
description: POMP siRNA reduced proteasome subunits and prolonged POMP silencing induced CHOP, consistent with unfolded-protein-response activation. This directly supports Pomp loss causing proteasome insufficiency and ER/proteotoxic stress.

citation: Obeng EA, Carlson LM, Gutman DM, Harrington WJ, Lee KP, Boise LH. Proteasome inhibitors induce a terminal unfolded protein response in multiple myeloma cells. Blood. 2006;107(12):4907-4916. doi:10.1182/blood-2005-08-3531.
description: This work showed that proteasome inhibition rapidly activates a PERK-ATF4-CHOP unfolded-protein-response branch. It supports a proteasome-impairment bridge for PSMB4 responses when Ddit3/Atf4 and heat-shock or ubiquitin-stress genes increase.

citation: Lewis CA, Griffiths B, Santos CR, Pende M, Schulze A. Regulation of the SREBP transcription factors by mTORC1. Biochemical Society Transactions. 2011;39(2):495-499. doi:10.1042/BST0390495.
description: This review summarizes data linking mTORC1 activation to SREBP-driven fatty-acid and cholesterol gene expression. Together with known TSC2 repression of mTORC1, it supports interpreting Tsc2-loss sterol-gene induction as mTORC1/SREBP activation.

citation: Lu W, Hagiwara D, Morishita Y, Tochiya M, Azuma Y, Suga H, Goto M, Banno R, Sugimura Y, Oyadomari S, Mori K, Arima H. Unfolded protein response in hypothalamic cultures of wild-type and ATF6alpha-knockout mice. Neuroscience Letters. 2016;612:199-204. doi:10.1016/j.neulet.2015.12.031.
description: The SERCA inhibitor thapsigargin induced BiP, Xbp1 splicing, Atf4, Chop, and ERAD genes in mouse hypothalamic cultures. This is a specific ER-calcium/SERCA bridge for Atp2a2 loss but remains pharmacologic and pan-SERCA rather than Atp2a2-specific.
